scope: Initial F09 shared bar candidate/reference/all tests and direct legacy callers; frozen protocol/design/all 31 golden cases read before candidate review

suspicions_investigated.imported_view_rows_hash_no_op: Confirmed. restore compares a hash then executes pass. Valid imported view ordering can differ from admission sorting, so replacing pass with raise without canonicalizing row order would reject valid restarts. A no-publication imported checkpoint with rows_hash changed still canonical-roundtrips and is accepted.
suspicions_investigated.per_query_full_event_scan_hidden_by_coun: Confirmed. query reconstructs ats from every captured Trade for every clock. _check_capture also digests every retained admission per query. capture.source_visits only counts len(events), and query work counts summary composition, omitting both scans/hash walks.
suspicions_investigated.carry_after_unknown_signs: Confirmed numerical defect in both candidate and reference. An unknown-side threshold bar followed by a known-side bar updates carry by known signed mass as though unknown mass were zero. The next bar can expose exact CVD OHLC from that invented opening. Activity partition itself can remain available; only carried CVD anchor must stay unknown until reset.

findings.finding: Imported rows_hash validation is a no-op and imported view metadata is assigned directly from decoded JSON without reconstructing its interval/cut/correction contract. Restore can accept changed rows_hash with no publications; malformed correction scope/counts can be admitted as retained evidence.
findings.repair: Normalize imported source rows to one explicit canonical order for hashing, validate view interval/cut/correction uniqueness/types/scope/bounds, and reject a mismatched retained hash. Add valid reordered-view and no-publication tamper tests.

findings.finding: Each query scans all event timestamps and rehashes the complete admission prefix before binary search. Each capture also reconstructs admissions, all leaf summaries and block-key hashes even when blocks are cached. The declared four-versus-twelve small source visits and 4096-versus32768 workload counters omit those physical source traversals.
findings.repair: Retain an immutable timestamp/index and precomputed immutable prefix proof in the capture; validate ownership/cursor without rewalking source rows. Count capture reconstruction, hashing, leaf creation, block construction and query/index work honestly. Keep build and query timing separate.

findings.finding: carry += pending.signed treats unknown signs as zero. Example events threshold1: unknown side size3 then buy size2. The second bar receives opening0 and exact CVD [0,2,0,2], although the true opening lies in [-3,3]. The literal independently traverses rows but duplicates the same wrong carry rule.
findings.repair: Carry an explicitly uncertain anchor after unknown signed mass; preserve available count/volume partitions while declining exact anchored CVD, and reset only on a named reset. Add unknown-first-block/known-next-block and reset-restores-zero cases in both implementations.

findings.finding: Read-only public properties do not protect reassignment/deletion of _domain/_definitions/_limits. Several public output dataclasses have no constructor validation. A replaced SharedBar can claim final=True via state='final', complete coverage, arbitrary publication or a forged summary and reach confirm_final_bars/opportunity_witness without retained publication proof.
findings.repair: Freeze admitted configuration slots and validate typed immutable public output records. Sanctioned downstream factories should require a factory-certified valid publication or reconstructible evidence, with replace/mutable nested inputs and forged finality/coverage assertions.

findings.finding: WindowCoverage accepts tuple elements that are mutable lists and does not apply timestamp/exact-int validation to each endpoint. WindowCoverage(..., observed_intervals=([0,10],), ...) can be mutated after request admission, changing coverage used by a supposedly immutable WindowRequest. Bool/float span endpoints can also pass comparisons.
findings.repair: Require immutable exact endpoint pairs, timestamp each endpoint, and strictly validate source/instrument identities. Re-read unchanged direct coverage consumers and add nested-mutation and bool/float interval cases.

findings.location: multiresolution.py:publish_activity; protocol one-pass materialization; tests B26
findings.finding: The API materializes one activity definition per call and traverses every event again for each clock. The registered benchmark exercises only time queries, so it does not establish the promised shared one-pass count/volume/range materialization under multiple active clocks.
findings.repair: Provide a bounded multi-definition whole-event dispatch or explicitly retain/count the per-clock work without claiming one shared pass. Add matched mixed-clock outputs and source/composition counters in the single registered finite workload; do not add repetitions or threshold searches.

findings.finding: Activity publication has no per-definition observation-cut/prefix regression check, unlike publish_window. An old capture can be published after a corrected/current capture at a later published_at and then become the newest value for an unchanged activity bar_id. Activity revision is always0, so version sequencing relies solely on insertion order.
findings.repair: Enforce monotone captured evidence for repeated activity materializations and retain explicit revision/publication order, while preserving saved historical captures as immutable audit evidence. Test old-capture publication after a correction and same-cut later admissions.

findings.finding: prefix_id hashes all admissions through cursor including entries whose known_at is after the captured cut. Adding/deleting an unavailable future suffix therefore changes a newly captured old-cut prefix ID and output version despite identical eligible events/corrections. B16 tests only an already stored publication, so it misses the stronger exact old-cut prefix invariant.
findings.repair: Separate admission cursor provenance from the causal eligible input identity or explicitly derive a cut-filtered prefix hash. Test reconstructing the same old cut after future additions/deletions and after same-cut later admission, retaining the intended distinction.

findings.finding: Activity end uses summary.last_at + 1 without timestamp validation on SharedBar. An otherwise valid Trade at maximum int64 time creates an out-of-domain endpoint. Public SharedBar also does not enforce interval nonemptiness, min-known/publication order, or valid state/revision types.
findings.repair: Validate computed endpoints and all publication scalar invariants before mutating retained state; reject an unrepresentable exclusive endpoint atomically. Include max-clock and malformed-publication cases.

findings.finding: The confirmation helper accepts any nonempty tuple of available complete bars, including duplicates, mixed definitions/instruments and arbitrary order. The B25 test passes one [0,4] aggregate under a descriptive 'two-right-final' name and therefore only proves a generic publication delay, not the frozen two-right-bar confirmation case.
findings.repair: Keep the generic helper honestly named/scoped or bind a declared confirmation rule to distinct ordered compatible bars. Exercise actual two-right-final evidence for the frozen thin fixture without claiming a hidden source predictor.

findings.finding: An explicit body_envelope is only checked against wick extrema, so a coarse bar with open100/close110 can claim body_envelope=(105,106). The merged result then purports to preserve a constituent body envelope that omits the supplied bar's endpoint bodies. Signed endpoint also reports buy-sell when unknown volume is positive without retaining endpoint bounds in CoarseAggregate.
findings.repair: Require an explicit constituent envelope to include the aggregate endpoints where those are known, and preserve signed support/unknown mass or expose bounds rather than an unqualified true endpoint when signs are incomplete. Add malformed envelope and unknown-side coarse cases.

findings.finding: Auxiliary public paths have weaker validation than shared trade admission: allocations do not revalidate original Trade clock/history/price contract, part_index and known_at equality can accept bool aliases, and quote bounds have no declared cardinality ceiling. These paths can undermine the stated exact immutable finite input contract even though ordinary Trade admission rejects allocations.
findings.repair: Apply exact typed/scalar checks and finite ceilings consistently to these auxiliary records/factories, retaining the distinction from independent trades. Add malformed bool/index/clock and over-bound auxiliary fixtures.

findings.finding: The activity parity helper compares forming summary only, omitting forming carry/epoch/state/overshoot and all per-bar interval/publication/correction/block lineage. There are no max-clock/max-publication/reset overflow atomic tests, activity checkpoint tamper/suffix tests, imported hash tamper tests or exact signed-order boundary permutations beyond simple examples.
findings.repair: Compare complete supported output/lineage fields and cover each declared limit/refusal path, valid activity restarts, reset placement, known/unknown carry and imported source evidence within the same registered suite.

findings.finding: Merging summaries repeatedly concatenates full event_ids/content_versions tuples and forms set intersections. Time queries still scan every block; activity pending merges can become quadratic in source identity copying for high thresholds. The workload reports compositions but not copied identity/source metadata volume, so it should not imply sublinear total work solely from summary count.
findings.repair: Use bounded indexed/range evidence or report this retained metadata work explicitly. The one toy timing may still pass without a speedup, but the comparison should distinguish arithmetic sharing from lineage copying and full construction costs.

known_legacy_findings_confirmed_not_new: Legacy BarEngine and ActivityBars configuration/published collections remain mutable; the newly authored legacy immutability assertions currently fail by inspection.
Legacy ActivityBars.restore verifies mass/partition but not first crossing or reset/completion reason reconstruction; authored tamper assertions currently fail by inspection.

Legacy BarEngine.restore accepts internally consistent altered volume/price fields without reconstructing retained request/coverage/watermark/input prefix. The new volume-tamper assertion currently fails by inspection.
Legacy repeated pending sums and independent scans remain as the limited baseline. Preserve direct BarEngine.ledger.correct caller compatibility during the consolidated repair.
non_findings: Time finality is indirectly protected by Watermark.known_at >= through_event_at and watermark.known_at <= capture.cut; the absence of a separate capture.cut >= request.end test is not itself a finality bug.
Whole-event oversized volume and high-minus-low range thresholds are arithmetically correct for known ordered inputs; no splitting is performed.
The ordered merge tie logic preserves ambiguous common endpoints only when tied prices agree, and refuses explicitly reversed ordered block boundaries.
Saved admission cursors in ordinary published checkpoints correctly reconstruct a publication made from a capture taken before a same-cut later admission, subject to the other validation findings.

No F09 production consumer is yet wired to the new module beyond the new tests. Legacy pivot, TransactionTapeView bar reference, object fixtures and existing bar tests were reviewed to preserve their interfaces.
next_step: Combine with root's full batch findings, then authorize the single consolidated repair and later supervised registered worker.
